questions.question:
Select the number-pair in which the two numbers are related in the same way as are the two numbers of the following number-pair.

12 : 42
questions.solution:
The pattern followed here is,

Second Number = First number × 3 + 6

12 × 3 + 6 = 36 + 6 = 42

16 × 3 + 6 = 54 ≠ 53

15 × 3 + 6 = 51 ≠ 52

24 × 3 + 6 = 78 ≠ 82

8 × 3 + 6 = 30

Hence, 8 : 30 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set.

(3, 16, 5)
questions.solution:
The pattern followed here is,

2 × (First number + Last number)

3 + 5 = 8; 8 × 2 = 16

Similarly,

7 + 9 = 16; 16 × 2 = 32.

Hence, (7, 32, 9) is the correct answer.

questions.question:

questions.solution:
**Concept:**

*If one face is common in both the dice,*

*then write the number in a clockwise direction from it.*

*Equivalent position number become Opposite number pair to it.*

*Here,*

Here, 3-2-4 and 3-6-1 are the sequence.

(2 and 6 ), (1 and 4) and the remaining (3 and 5) become the opposite pair.

Thus, if 6 is at the bottom then 2 will be on the top.

Hence, **2 **is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Two statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

Some roads are streets

Some streets are lanes

**Conclusions:**

I. No road is a lane

II. All streets are lanes

III. Some lanes are roads

options.text: Only conclusions II and III follow
Either conclusions I or III follows

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram according to the information is,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ebc134d955a2eb1d6625dd6215ae64552786a87d14d3dddc6f23b947817f779e.png] 

No road is a lane → False, it is possible but not definite.

All streets are lanes → False, it is possible but not definite.

Some lanes are roads → False, it is possible but not definite.

Conclusion I and III are complementary pairs

Hence, either conclusions I or III follows.

questions.question: The ratio of the present age of Mitali to that of Shabnam is 4 : 7. If the difference between the present age of Shabnam and the age of Mitali after 5 years will be 13 years, then what is the sum of the present ages of Mitali and shabnam?
questions.solution:
Let the present age of Mitali and Shabnam be 4x and 7x.

Mitali’s age after 5 years will be 4x + 5,

The difference between present age of Shabnam and Mitali’s age after 5 years = 7x - (4x + 5) = 13

7x - 4x - 5 = 13

3x = 13 + 5

3x = 18

x = 6

Hence present ages of Mitali and Shabnam will be 24 and 42.

Sum of the present age of Mitali and Shabnam = 24 + 42 = 66

Hence, 66 is the correct answer.
